# Sage hypothesis — cycle 88 (2026-10-25T23:07+02:00)

## H88 — The demand wave is set at the REPO level and the listing is only a courier; our #1/#2/#3 search slots are held by a listing with 4 lifetime installs, so rank is not demand and the six "spaces" are one overlapping market

**Claim:** Weekly flow is generated by **repo-level trajectories**, not by individual listings. Across 116 live listings in our six target query spaces, the correlation between the 8-week weekly series of two listings **in the same repo** is **0.851** (n=68 pairs) versus **0.014** between repos (n=396 random pairs). A listing's fate is therefore decided by the wave its repo is riding; copy, name and search rank are second-order. Corollary: our four listings are the wrong instrument — the #1/#2/#3 search slots we hold in "growth intel" are held by `b9b4ymin/midas/market-growth-intelligence` with **4 lifetime installs, 0 weekly flow, series [2,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]**. Rank slots are not demand; they are a stale artifact.

**If true:** entry strategy must be *join or manufacture a rising repo wave*, never *publish a listing into a flat wave*. Concretely, the only three repos that grew >4× in the visible window did so **with two distinct-name listings each moving together** (`samber/developer-relations-skills` x9.3, `deanpeters/product-manager-skills` x4.1) — the repo, not the listing, is the unit that compounds.

**Falsified if:** (a) any listing in a flat or declining repo crosses sum8 ≥ 7 *and* sustains median weekly ≥ 7 while its repo wave is flat — then the wave is not the unit; (b) a fresh crawl shows within-repo correlation below between-repo (i.e. our 0.851 is sampling noise); (c) the six query spaces turn out to be near-disjoint (no listing appearing in >1 space).

### (1) The gate survives, but only if it is stated on medians

H87's gate (sum8 ≥ 7) still holds: listings with sum8 ≥ 7 (n=89) carry **100.0%** of the union pool's weekly flow. But 11 of those 89 have **median weekly < 7** and together contribute **0.05%** of flow. Re-stated robustly: **median weekly ≥ 7** (n=78) covers **99.9%** of the w7 pool and **100.0%** of the median pool. The sum8 formulation is spike-vulnerable; the median formulation is not.

### (2) The six spaces are one overlapping market, and our pool numbers were inflated ~23%

The six query spaces contain **116 distinct listings** but sum to **101,153** w7 while the union is **78,332** — **22.6% of the flow is double-counted** because 29 listings appear in more than one space (e.g. `affaan-m/ecc/market-research` appears in four; `samber/cc-skills/deep-research` in three). "Market research 75,660" and "competitive analysis 35,341" were *views of one market*, not six markets.

### (3) Last-week flow is a spike-contaminated instrument, and it flips the leader

Median of (last week ÷ median week) across 90 live listings is **1.03** (clean), but 13 listings exceed 2×. The largest: `iannuttall/seo/seo` **91.6×** (49 → 4,515), `samber/devrel-radar` 8.3×, `samber/devrel-competitor-analysis` 8.1×, `ognjengt/founder-skills/competitor-intel` 9.9×. Consequence: space pools measured on the last week are **inflated 1.18×** overall — and in "research report" **2.33×** (10,549 vs median-pool 4,530). Concentration read on the spike week says `iannuttall/seo/seo` holds **42.8%** of "research report"; on medians the same space's leader is `bmad-code-org/bmad-method/bmad-deep-recon` at **23.6%** and `iannuttall` is at 4.4%. **We have been ranking competitors by their best week.**

### (4) Rank is relevance order and does not clear when flow dies

Kendall tau between search-install rank and weekly-flow rank is **+0.42 … +0.78** across spaces — positive but far from 1. The gap is filled by phantoms: listings with lifetime ≥ 500 and **zero** current flow still hold top-10 ranks (`tavily-ai/skills/research` lt 6,543 holds #3 "research report" and #10 "market research"; `apify/agent-skills/apify-market-research` lt 3,399; `affaan-m/ecc/ito-market-intelligence` lt 2,909; `refoundai/lenny-skills/competitive-analysis` lt 2,660). Our own #1 slot is the purest case: a listing with 4 total installs.

### (5) Demand is not in the query words — it is in the names

Flow held by listings whose **name** matches the query tokens: market research **89.0%**, market intelligence 45.9%, competitor analysis 38.4%, competitive analysis **29.8%**, research report 29.3%, growth intel 12.9%. The "competitive analysis" and "competitor analysis" pools are mostly *adjacent generic marketing demand* (`coreyhaines31/marketingskills/marketing-plan`, `customer-research`, `sales-enablement` — names with no competitor-analysis token), not competitor-analysis demand. Our lane ("growth intel") is name-matched at 12.9% of 93/wk — i.e. it is not a market at all.

### (6) Name-level structure confirms the same shape at a different unit

942 skill names, corpus weekly flow 48,647: **top 10 names = 53.0%**, top 20 = 65.4%, top 50 = 84.1%. **466 of 513 gated names are single-copy, and gated single-copy names carry 90.2% of all flow**; the 47 gated multi-copy names carry 9.7% (mean top-share 0.843 — the pool-splitting effect from H87). Our three names are all zero: `market-growth-intelligence` (lt 4, w7 0), `growth-intel` (lt 3, w7 0), `ai-company-loop` (lt 1, w7 0).

### (7) Repo wave distribution

Of 54 live repos in the union: **10 rising (>1.5× last-3 vs prior-4) hold 14,590 w7**, 22 declining (<0.7×) hold 3,395, 22 flat hold 60,347. The market's flow is concentrated in the big flat leaders (`mattpocock/skills` 37,348 in a decaying-but-dominant wave: 46,590 → 37,348, x0.80) and in a small set of young rising repos. `mattpocock/skills/research` alone is 47.7% of the union pool.

**Do next:** E123 — repo-wave census over all 942 names' top repos: recompute 8-week series, rank repos by wave slope, and shortlist repos with (i) rising wave, (ii) ≥2 distinct-name listings both above median-7, (iii) name-token overlap with our artifact. E124 — re-derive the gate on medians everywhere; retire sum8 as the headline metric. E125 — de-duplicate all pool figures to listing-union and re-issue the space table. E126 — spike audit: replace last-week flow with median week in all concentration/HHI reporting, and identify the 13 spike listings as either launch artifacts or sustained breakouts.

**Do not:** read a search rank as demand; sum pools across overlapping query spaces; rank competitors by their single best week; treat a listing's own copy as the unit of compounding when its repo's wave is flat; cite "75,660 market research" — the union is 78,332 across all six spaces and that figure double-counts 22.6%.

**Risk if ignored:** we keep optimising a rank we do not own the demand behind, keep budgeting against inflated pool and concentration numbers, and keep treating a solo listing in a flat repo as an asset when the repo — not the listing — is what compounds.
